examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: В интернете = on the internet. International borrowing from English 'Internet' ('inter-' + 'network').

examples.trans: Look it up on the internet.
Look it up on the internet.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'sausage', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Осторожно, ты пронзил меня своей колбасой!
examples.trans: Careful, you impaled me with your sausage!

examples.text: Обидишь Настю, я из тебя колбасу сделаю.
examples.trans: If you hurt Nastya, I will turn you into sausage.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
In a mistaken or improper manner. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'правильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Луи, ты меня совсем неправильно понял!

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
He didn't want to offend anyone.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. And what are you doing here?

meanings.note: fleeting е in all declined forms: отца, отцу...

examples.text: Твой отец когда-то назвал меня очкариком.
examples.trans: Your father once called me four-eyes.
My father works at a factory.

examples.text: Слушай, эти детские клички такие прилипчивые. Твой отец когда-то назвал меня очкариком.
examples.trans: Listen, these childhood nicknames really stick. Your father once called me four-eyes.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.
